harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Resolved INC-042. Loki identified node2 at 2026-09-02T14:14:11.666881502Z as the origin, caused by the invalid nginx directive `upstream_timeoutx`. Corrected it to `send_timeout`, restored all tiers and the node1 end-to-end path, preserved catalog data and Loki history, and created `/root/INC-042-report.txt`. All four nodes passed sequential restart-and-recovery verification.
actions_performed: Queried Grafana health and Loki incident streams on node1
Corrected only the faulty node2 nginx directive and retained a rollback copy
Restored catalog-api, orders-api, checkout-api, and the complete node1 request path
Created and restart-verified the incident report on node1
Restarted node4, node3, node2, then node1 individually and verified recovery after each

evidence.requirement: Identify the originating fault using node1 observability
evidence.summary: Grafana was healthy; Loki showed node2's configuration error at Unix nanoseconds 1788358451666881502 before the node3 and node4 dependency errors.

evidence.requirement: Correct the originating fault without unrelated configuration changes
evidence.summary: A checksum-matched rollback copy was retained; the diff contains only `upstream_timeoutx 5s` → `send_timeout 5s`, and nginx validation succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Restore every tier and the complete request path
evidence.summary: Final direct checks show active nginx services, valid configurations, healthy catalog/orders/checkout paths, and a healthy node1 entry path.

evidence.requirement: Preserve incident history and catalog data
evidence.summary: Catalog hashes and records are unchanged across repair and restart; all three original Loki events remain queryable.

evidence.requirement: Record the incident report on node1
evidence.summary: The report contains the originating node, exact earliest Loki timestamp, initiating error, and correction, and persisted across node1's reboot.
